title: VPC post-deploy conformance + warmup executor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight, configurable post-deploy executor that runs after Terraform applies for VPC/private deployments. The executor will run API readiness probes, model inference smoke tests, and targeted model load verification (warmup). Goals: reduce customer incidents from cold-start failures, validate network/RBAC surface after IaC changes, and produce artifactable evidence (logs/JSON reports) for release signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Executor can be invoked from CI/CD (Terraform apply -> executor hook) and returns a structured JSON report
API readiness probe passes against control plane and inference endpoints within configured timeouts
Smoke test runs at least 3 model configs (small, med, large) and verifies token-level response and latency thresholds
Warmup procedure loads model KV cache and performs a repeat inference to show median latency improvement
Failure modes are classified (transient, config, capacity) and mapped to automated remediation or clear follow-up steps
Artifacts (s3/GCS) with logs and a human-readable summary are created and linked in the deployment run
steps: Design executor config schema (timeout, models, endpoints, retry policy)
Add Terraform null_resource hook to trigger post-deploy executor with secure credentials
Implement API readiness checks: /health, auth sanity, TLS handshake verification
Implement model smoke runner: small synthetic prompts + deterministic validation predicates
Implement warmup sequence: progressive KV cache load, single-token streaming validation
Create structured JSON report schema and artifact uploader (S3/GCS/Artifact service)
Add failure classification mapping to runbook and automated Slack/GitOps alerts
Integrate with CI: example GitHub Actions workflow and retry logic
notes: Trade-off: full load testing is expensive; executor focuses on functional smoke + targeted warmup rather than full-scale perf tests
We will not ship heavy synthetic load (100% traffic) in default executor; opt-in mode will exist for dedicated capacity customers
Consider adding an opt-in retry window for autoscaling to absorb warmup spikes (follow-up ticket)
